key_idea: A value at a binary-search midpoint is found iff it lies strictly between the largest pivot where the search went right and the smallest pivot where it went left along its path.
sketch: Generate the sequence with 64-bit arithmetic (a and x up to 2^31). Traverse the implicit binary search tree of index ranges (lo,hi) carrying the open interval (mn,mx) of values that would be routed here; the midpoint counts if mn < x[mid] < mx, then recurse left with mx=min(mx,x[mid]) and right with mn=max(mn,x[mid]). This is O(n) with an explicit stack; simulating a search for each value in O(n log n) also passes. Pitfall: overflow in a*x and using exactly mid=(lo+hi)/2.
